name: Service charges, leaseholder accounts and major works consultation
one_line: The organizational situation of SPLITTING A BUILDING'S RUNNING COSTS AMONG THE PEOPLE WHO LIVE IN IT: a managing agent budgets what the block will cost next year, demands each flat's apportioned share on fixed dates, spends the money, has the year certified by an accountant, and consults everybody formally before spending a large sum on the roof. The organizing anchor is the BUILDING plus a SERVICE CHARGE YEAR, and the row's defining property is that every document exists in two versions of itself - the whole building's, and one leaseholder's share of it - which is what makes it a filing situation rather than a document type. Absorbs the legacy row prop.service-charge (ROW). Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

an apportionment structure: a schedule of costs by heading - insurance, cleaning, lifts, grounds, management fee, reserve fund - against a percentage or fraction attributed to each unit, with the fractions summing across the building. A cost table split by a fixed share per flat is the discriminating shape and it exists in no other document in this catalogue. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a demand structure: a payment demand for a stated period naming a unit, an amount, a due date, and - distinctively - a block of prescribed statutory wording about the recipient's rights, printed on the face of the demand.

a service-charge year structure: a budget for a period, followed by a year-end account for the SAME period reconciling estimated against actual with a balancing charge or credit. The estimate-then-reconcile pair over a fixed year is what separates this from any ordinary bill.
an accountant's certificate: a signed statement that the year's account presents the costs incurred, addressed to leaseholders rather than to a company's members.

a consultation notice structure: a formal notice of intention to carry out works, an invitation to comment within a stated period, a statement of estimates naming contractors and prices, and a notice of the reason for the choice made. A staged, statutory-shaped consultation about spending exists in no other row here.
a reserve or sinking fund statement: a balance carried across years, with contributions and drawdowns - a fund belonging to a building rather than to a person.
a resale or management pack: a bundle answering a buyer's questions about charges, arrears, works planned and disputes, assembled for one flat at one moment.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

which side of the demand the file is on. The agent's file, the freeholder's file, the residents' company's file and one leaseholder's file all contain the same budget and the same accounts, and only purpose separates them. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
separating an estimated demand from the balancing account for the same year, when both are one-page documents naming the same period and different amounts.
distinguishing a service charge from ground rent, from a buildings insurance recharge and from a major works levy, which arrive together and are legally different things.
recognising a consultation notice as a stage in a sequence rather than a standalone letter, when the earlier stages are missing from the corpus.
reading a dispute out of correspondence where the operative content is a challenge to reasonableness rather than a refusal to pay.

a management pack that is purpose-coherent and content-incoherent: accounts, a budget, an insurance schedule, arrears figures and a works history. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: a building or unit address alone. Every demand, every account, every bill and every neighbouring row carries one, and it does not say whether the file is the building's or one flat's. Read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”
a managing agent's or freeholder's organisation name alone.
a money total or a percentage alone: apportionments, interest, VAT and arrears all print as percentages.
the words charge, demand, statement or account alone - the most generic financial document words in the corpus.

a bare 4-digit number, as likely a unit reference, a scheme number or a fund balance fragment as a year - and a service charge year frequently does not run to the calendar, which makes a stray four-digit token especially misleading here.

membership in a download session that pulled a whole management portal folder at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

an extension or a source_type alone - “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”

work_types: major works specification and cost report
buildings insurance schedule for the block
grouping_reasons: one service charge year for one building: the budget, the demands issued under it, the year-end accounts and the balancing statement - which only make sense as a set, because the account exists to reconcile the budget.

one major works consultation across its stages: notice of intention, estimates, observations, award, and the works cost that lands in a later year's account. Purpose-coherent, content-incoherent, and spread across two or three service charge years.

one unit's charges across years, which is how a leaseholder files and how an agent does not - the second axis, and the one that tempts the product to carry a building-level total onto a single flat's record. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
a resale pack as a bundle assembled for one flat at one moment, which dissolves after the sale.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single demand received by a leaseholder with no accounts around it is a transactional record.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: construction_property declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the anchor is the BUILDING or scheme, then the service charge year, then the document stage - budget, demands, accounts, consultation. The unit belongs BELOW the year on the professional side, because an agent's question is always about a building in a year and only then about a flat; a leaseholder's tree inverts it, and that inversion is the seam with finance.hoa-residents-association rather than a defect in this order. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” - a balancing charge is unintelligible without the budget it reconciles. Not time-first at the top: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - though the service charge YEAR is the load-bearing second level, and it is worth recording that it frequently does not run to the calendar, so a year dimension here is a named accounting period and not a date. Privacy caveat specific to this row: arrears schedules name individual residents and what they owe, consultation and dispute correspondence names them taking positions against their neighbours, and a block's records are a list of who lives where. None of that should acquire automatic internal depth or reach a model prompt by default. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The row's defining seam, and it is the professional/householder seam this whole schema sits on, seen from the block side. That row holds the association-to-member relationship and a resident's own dues, assessments, meeting papers and correspondence; this row holds the managing agent's or freeholder's administration of a building's costs. The discriminating evidence: an apportionment schedule across a whole building, a budget-and-certified-accounts pair for a service charge year, or a consultation sequence supports this row; a single member's account, dues notices, meeting papers and association governance supports the association row. A unit address, an agent's name or a money figure counts for neither - stated in that row's own terms so the pair reads consistently.

The nearest sibling on this schema: the same agent, the same building, the same file. The discriminating evidence: the money cycle - budget, demand, account, consultation on spending - supports this row; the operational management of the building, its contractors, its compliance and its residents' day-to-day matters supports the block row. The two are genuinely one folder in practice, and the split is by function rather than by file.

The lease is what creates the charge and fixes the apportionment, and ground rent arrives beside the service charge as a legally different payment under the same instrument. The discriminating evidence: party recitals, covenants, a term and an execution block identify the lease as legal material - that row's own stated signal; a demand or an account issued under it supports this row.

A leaseholder's own copies of demands and accounts are household property administration. The discriminating evidence: a household's retained records of its own home supports the household row; a building-wide administration file supports this row. Reciprocal to the seam that row already draws against finance.hoa-residents-association.

Major works produce a construction contract inside a service charge, so the same roof job generates valuations here and consultation notices there. The discriminating evidence: the contractual payment cycle with a contractor supports the final-account row; the consultation with, and recharge to, leaseholders supports this row.

An agent's own ledger, client account and fee income sit beside the building's money and must not be mixed with it. The discriminating evidence: the agent's own revenue and accounting supports bookkeeping; money held and spent on behalf of a building supports this row.

The block buildings insurance schedule is recharged through the service charge and is also an insurance record. The discriminating evidence: a policy, a schedule and a claim history supports the insurance row; the recharge and its apportionment supports this row.

The resale or management pack is a member of a conveyancing transaction as well as an output of this row. The discriminating evidence: the transaction pack around a property supports the sale row; the building's own charge records support this row. Reciprocal to the fixture authored there.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a standalone budget, set of accounts or consultation notice with a durable purpose and no accepted year group. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The correct home for the transactional side this row must not absorb - an isolated demand, reminder or payment confirmation, which is the most common single file in this situation. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

The correct home for an arrears schedule or a dispute file with no accepted group - a list of named neighbours and what they owe. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The cautious outcome for a demand whose period OCR lost, or a challenge thread whose status is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The safe outcome for a management portal export or a password-protected resale pack. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: A block's charge file is a register of who lives where and how they are doing. Arrears schedules name individual residents against what they owe and how long they have owed it; consultation and challenge correspondence names neighbours taking positions against each other and against the agent; and the apportionment schedule, harmlessly, is a map of every flat in the building. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and account statements and private correspondence fall inside it. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” The concrete risk in this row is the group summary: a building's year assembled into one view republishes every resident's payment record in one place. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether this row and construction_property.block-management should be one row rather than two. In practice they are one folder: the same managing agent, the same building, the same year, and the roof works appear in both as a cost and as a project. This row is written as the MONEY cycle - budget, demand, account, consultation on spending - and concedes operations, contractors, compliance and resident matters to the block row, but the split is by function and not by file, and a user filing a block would not naturally make it. The other agent owns that row and the collision is authored so the question is visible from both sides; whether to merge is Joseph's. A second question, on the other flank: a leaseholder's own copies of these documents are finance.hoa-residents-association's or finance.household-property's, and a single scanned demand with nothing around it should not activate this professional row at all - the fixture says so, but where exactly the threshold sits between one demand and a building's file is the same judgement NJ-CP-13 raises about transactions, and it is Joseph's for the same reason.
